dossier.summary: OpenCode CLI v1.18.11 is represented as an exact immutable source release for the terminal CLI/TUI, with unresolved installed artifact and runtime. Current publisher sources separately describe Build and Plan modes, configurable permissions and tools, OpenCode Zen versus external providers, model selection, sharing and an explicit no-sandbox limitation; none is treated as observed behavior.

releaseContext.statement: Anomaly Innovations, Inc.'s OpenCode repository published immutable release v1.18.11 on 2026-08-01 at source revision 012c2f57f976489d88bd4598a056b4bdcdd428ee. Current documentation and policies are rolling-current and are not silently applied to that exact release.

limitations: All product claims are attributed to official OpenCode sources; no product behavior was observed.
No OpenCode binary, package, container, source checkout, dependency set or model service was downloaded, installed, hashed or run.
The exact record is limited to the CLI/TUI; desktop, IDE, SDK and unrelated server surfaces are excluded.
Current documentation and policies may postdate v1.18.11 and remain rolling-current rather than exact-version receipts.
The exact tagged source and current agent documentation differ in their Plan-mode permission descriptions; this is preserved as a resolved version/time scope difference.
OpenCode Zen and external providers remain separate routes with separate service revisions and data-policy applicability.
The publisher says OpenCode is not sandboxed and permissions are not a security boundary; no independent security validation was performed.
No capability quality, safety, privacy, performance or suitability conclusion is supported.

propositions.question: Which OpenCode release and surface are pinned?
propositions.status: v1.18.11 tag and source revision known
propositions.answer: The immutable v1.18.11 release and source revision are exact; the record is limited to the terminal CLI/TUI.
propositions.whyItMatters: Desktop, IDE and other related surfaces must not inherit this evidence.

propositions.question: Which artifact and environment ran?
propositions.answer: Publisher sources document several distribution paths, but no package, binary, image, platform or runtime was observed.
propositions.whyItMatters: A source tag does not establish an installed artifact or dependency graph.

propositions.question: Do Build or Plan boundaries apply?
propositions.answer: Exact v1.18.11 source and current docs both separate Build and Plan, but their Plan permission descriptions differ and remain scoped by version/time.
propositions.whyItMatters: The catalog must not collapse modes or transfer rolling defaults to the exact release.

propositions.question: Which actions require approval?
propositions.answer: Current docs define ordered allow, ask and deny rules with per-agent and pattern-specific overrides.
propositions.whyItMatters: Tool authority depends on the effective merged policy, not the client version alone.

propositions.question: Which tool paths can be available?
propositions.status: Built-in, custom and MCP paths documented
propositions.answer: Current docs list built-in file, shell, web and related tools plus custom tools and MCP servers, all subject to configuration and permissions.
propositions.whyItMatters: Documented availability is not evidence that a tool was enabled or used.

propositions.question: Which provider and model produced output?
propositions.answer: OpenCode Zen, external hosted providers and local providers are separate alternatives; exact provider, model and service revisions are unknown.
propositions.whyItMatters: The CLI release does not freeze the inference backend.

propositions.question: Is local execution sandboxed?
propositions.answer: The publisher states that OpenCode itself is not sandboxed and that permissions are not a security boundary; external OS, container or VM isolation is a separate user-selected path.
propositions.whyItMatters: Approval UX and security isolation cannot be treated as the same control.

propositions.question: Where can model requests and session data go?
propositions.answer: Zen has model-dependent policy claims; external-provider terms remain separate; session sharing can be manual, automatic or disabled.
propositions.whyItMatters: Provider routing and public session sharing are distinct data destinations.

propositions.question: Was OpenCode v1.18.11 independently evaluated here?
propositions.answer: No public evaluation entry passed the exact release, model, permission, mode, tool, disclosure and artifact gates into this dossier.
propositions.whyItMatters: Publisher documentation is attribution, not independent observed behavior.
